name: Clozapine
short: Gold standard for treatment-resistant schizophrenia; the only antipsychotic shown to reduce suicide.
mechanism: A 5HT2A/D2 antagonist whose many other binding properties are mostly **more potent than D2** (α1, 5HT2B, M1, H1, 5HT2A, 5HT6, 5HT2C, M4 and others; Figure 5-43). It occupies **fewer D2 receptors** than other drugs at therapeutic doses, so its gold-standard efficacy probably comes from an unknown **non-D2** mechanism.
uses: May help **aggression and violence** in psychotic patients (Chapter 4)

facts.text: With high doses of standard drugs for schizophrenia, may help **psychotic or impulsive violence**; behavioral measures help impulsive violence and organized violence may need confinement.

Table 5-2 lists side effects needing expert management: neutropenia, constipation/paralytic ileus, sedation/orthostasis/tachycardia, sialorrhea, seizures, weight gain/dyslipidemia/hyperglycemia, myocarditis/cardiomyopathy/interstitial nephritis, DRESS/serositis.
One of the three agents with the widest 5HT2A–D2 separation and **D2 occupancy below 60%** at antipsychotic doses.
Among the agents with the lowest DIP, attributed to robust **α1 + 5HT2A** antagonism.

targets.note: Action not specified in the book

pearls: Little motor effect, **no prolactin** elevation, does not seem to cause TD
Underused; finger-stick point-of-care counts and **plasma levels** help

updates.title: Clozapine REMS removed
updates.text: The FDA eliminated the clozapine REMS in 2025; ANC reporting to a REMS program is no longer required before dispensing, but the FDA still advises ANC monitoring per the prescribing information.

name: Olanzapine
short: Probably the next most effective after clozapine; high metabolic risk.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** whose strongest binding is at **H1 and 5HT2A** (Figure 5-44). **5HT2C** antagonism may help mood and cognition, and with H1 antagonism contributes to **weight gain**. Strong muscarinic binding.
uses: **IM** agitation in schizophrenia or bipolar mania
With **fluoxetine**: bipolar depression and treatment-resistant unipolar depression (US)
pearls: Often used at **higher** doses than approved, guided by plasma levels
Forms: orally disintegrating, acute IM, **4-week depot**; inhaled form in development
Combination with **samidorphan** to limit weight gain

facts.text: Widely considered, by clinical experience rather than definitive trials, the **next most effective** after clozapine; 5HT2C plus weaker α2 antagonism, especially with fluoxetine’s 5HT2C antagonism, may explain efficacy in depression.

Table 7-1: mania, maintenance; with **fluoxetine** for bipolar depression and treatment-resistant MDD; post hoc evidence in mania with mixed features. The combination acts as a potent SERT/5HT2C inhibitor but causes weight gain.
Used cautiously **off-label** for agitation/psychosis in dementia despite the boxed warning for stroke and death.

updates.title: Olanzapine–samidorphan approved
updates.text: Olanzapine combined with the μ-opioid antagonist samidorphan (Lybalvi) was approved for schizophrenia and bipolar I disorder in May 2021.

name: Quetiapine
short: A “different drug at different doses”: sleep at 50 mg, depression at 300 mg, psychosis at 800 mg.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with **weak D2** binding. Its net actions combine the parent drug and the active metabolite **norquetiapine**, which adds **NET inhibition**; together they have **5HT7, 5HT2C and α2** antagonism and **5HT1A** partial agonism (Figure 5-45). Its most potent action is **H1** antagonism.
uses: **Bipolar depression**; **augmentation** of SSRIs/SNRIs in unipolar depression (US)
Often used for insomnia (not approved), anxiety, **Parkinson’s disease psychosis**, or as an adjunct

sideEffects.e: Virtually no motor effects or prolactin elevation

pearls: **Baby Bear 50 mg**: H1 only; **Mama Bear 300 mg**: antidepressant mix; **Papa Bear 800 mg**: saturates H1 and 5HT2A, inconsistent >60% D2 occupancy

facts.text: Goldilocks and the three bears: different pharmacology at 50, 300 and 800 mg (Figure 5-46). Low D2 occupancy (< 60%) at antipsychotic doses.
Table 7-1: mania, maintenance, **bipolar depression** and **adjunct for MDD**; antidepressant action may come from norquetiapine at NET and 5HT2C plus 5HT2A, 5HT7, α2A antagonism and 5HT1A agonism.
Sedating via H1 (with other) blockade; mirtazapine and chlorpromazine fall in the “still too hot” (hangover) category of Figure 10-41C.
The book does **not** list quetiapine among the D2 blockers used off-label in dementia.

name: Asenapine
short: Sublingual pine related to mirtazapine; usable as a rapid oral PRN.
mechanism: Structurally related to **mirtazapine** and shares its **5HT2A, 5HT2C, H1 and α2** antagonism, plus **D2** antagonism and many other serotonin and dopamine actions (Figure 5-47). Antidepressant action is suggested, but only antipsychotic/antimanic action is proven.
uses: Rapid-acting **oral PRN** “top-up” instead of an injection

sideEffects.e: Moderate weight gain, metabolic and motor effects

pearls: **Not absorbed if swallowed**: sublingual, usually twice daily; no food or drink for **10 minutes**

facts.text: Rapid sublingual absorption gives rapid peak levels, unlike orally dissolving tablets that are absorbed later.
Table 7-1: approved for **bipolar mania** and **maintenance**; evidence in **mania with mixed features**.

name: Zotepine
short: Pine available in Japan and Europe; three times daily; possible seizure risk.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** that is also a **5HT2C, α1 and 5HT7** antagonist, a weak **5HT1A** partial agonist and a weak **NET** inhibitor, suggesting antidepressant potential not yet established (Figure 5-48).
uses: Schizophrenia (Japan and Europe; not the US)

facts.text: Less popular because it must be given **three times a day**.

name: Risperidone
short: The original “done”; raises prolactin even at low doses.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with a different structure and profile from the pines (Figure 5-49). **α2** antagonism may contribute to antidepressant action, but simultaneous **α1** antagonism can cancel it and causes orthostasis and sedation.
uses: Low-dose off-label use in dementia agitation/psychosis is controversial (**black box** warning)

sideEffects.via: D2 blockade not offset by its 5HT2A action

sideEffects.e: Moderate weight gain and dyslipidemia (especially in **children**)
Fewer motor effects at lower doses

pearls: Depot injections lasting **2 or 4 weeks**; monitor plasma levels of risperidone + paliperidone

facts.text: Some prefer it for children and adolescents; it may need twice-daily dosing at initiation (especially in children or the elderly) to avoid sedation and orthostasis.
Table 7-1: approved for **bipolar mania** and **maintenance**.
Used cautiously **off-label** for agitation/psychosis in dementia despite the boxed warning for stroke and death.

name: Paliperidone
short: Risperidone’s active metabolite: renally cleared, sustained release, long-interval injections.
mechanism: The active metabolite of risperidone, sharing its **5HT2A/D2** antagonism and binding (Figure 5-50). **Not hepatically metabolized** (urinary excretion), so few pharmacokinetic interactions.
uses: Long-acting injectable: **1-month and 3-month** (6-month in study at publication)

sideEffects.e: Moderate weight gain and metabolic risk
Perhaps less sedation, orthostasis and motor effects than risperidone (anecdotal)

pearls: Sustained-release oral form: **once daily**, but easily **underdosed**
LAI is easier to load and dose than risperidone’s

facts.text: Rapid absorption and high peaks of risperidone may cause some of its side effects; paliperidone’s controlled release removes these.

updates.title: Six-month injection approved
updates.text: A 6-month paliperidone palmitate long-acting injection (Invega Hafyera) was approved for adults with schizophrenia after adequate treatment with the 1- or 3-month formulations.

name: Ziprasidone
short: 5HT2A/D2 antagonist with little or no weight gain; take with food.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** that also binds 5HT1B/1D about as potently as D2, plus 5HT2C, 5HT7, D3, α1 and weak **NET and SERT** (Figure 5-51). It lacks the actions linked to weight gain, insulin resistance and significant sedation.

sideEffects.e: Little or no weight gain or metabolic effect

pearls: Short acting: more than once daily, **with food**
QTc concerns now seem **exaggerated**: no dose-dependent QTc prolongation, few drugs raise its levels

facts.text: Unlike iloperidone, zotepine, sertindole and amisulpride, ziprasidone does **not** cause dose-dependent QTc prolongation.
Table 7-1: approved for **bipolar mania** and **maintenance**; evidence in **mania with mixed features**.

name: Iloperidone
short: Simple profile with potent α1 antagonism: very low motor effects, slow titration.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with one of the **simplest** profiles, closest to a pure serotonin–dopamine antagonist; its most potent property is **α1 antagonism** (Figure 5-52).
uses: Schizophrenia/maintenance (US); often a **switch** agent in non-urgent settings
pearls: 18- to 33-hour half-life, but usually twice daily with **slow titration**, which delays onset

facts.text: Its distinguishing features are very low motor side effects, low dyslipidemia, moderate weight gain and potent α1 antagonism.
Among the agents with the lowest DIP, attributed to robust **α1 + 5HT2A** antagonism.

updates.title: Bipolar I indication
updates.text: Iloperidone was approved for acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder in adults in April 2024.
